findings.trigger: An installation whose web_config.json carries advanced_settings (the v1.1.x migration writes them there, and the loader's _legacy_advanced_settings reads them from there and nowhere else) goes through the automatic modular migration. migrate_web_configs_to_files writes web_ui.json deliberately WITHOUT advanced_settings and logs 'advanced_settings kept in web_config.json' (line 363); migrate_system_configs_to_files writes config.json without them; then cleanup_legacy_files_after_migration unlinks web_config.json (line 201). Result: every advanced setting (the env_* toggles, e.g. the Docker cache duration) falls back to its default while the log says 'Automatic modular migration completed successfully'. The only remaining copy is backup_<ts>/web_config.json, which nothing reads. The loader (config_loader_service.py:145-149, 206-213) still calls web_config.json a 'migration-only file' that serves as 'legacy fallback' - a file this class deletes.
findings.suggestion: Either copy advanced_settings into the new config.json inside migrate_web_configs_to_files (config.json is the live save target the loader prefers anyway) before the cleanup runs, or leave web_config.json out of the cleanup list. Then correct the log line and the loader comments to say where the values actually live.
findings.unsure_why: ConfigService (not in this section) may run its one-time fold BEFORE ensure_modular_structure and thereby copy the advanced settings into config.json first - but even then migrate_system_configs_to_files overwrites config.json (see F3). Whether any consumer other than the loader still holds the values, and whether the fold renames the v1 files so that no migration follows, I cannot see.

findings.trigger: A migrated installation whose legacy channels_config.json is still on disk (the docstring at lines 120-121 explicitly expects such installs: 'migrated before the marker existed', and no .modular_migration_complete marker exists for them). The operator removes the last channel in the panel; ChannelConfigService writes ALL_CHANNELS_REMOVED_MARKER and no <id>.json remains. On the next start needs_real_modular_migration() asks _modular_structure_is_complete(): channels_config.json exists and channels_dir has no *.json -> False -> the migration runs again. migrate_channels_to_files recreates every channel from the legacy file (the deliberately removed channels come back with their old permissions), default.json is overwritten, and migrate_system_configs_to_files/migrate_web_configs_to_files overwrite config.json and web_ui.json with the legacy values (see F3). The log reports success. has_real_modular_structure (config_loader_service.py:180-182) honours the marker; this twin check does not - the two have drifted.
findings.suggestion: In _modular_structure_is_complete treat (channels_dir / ALL_CHANNELS_REMOVED_MARKER).exists() as a populated channels target, exactly as has_real_modular_structure does; better, share one helper. Also write the completion marker for installs that answer 'complete' so the question is never asked again.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see how many installations still carry legacy files next to a complete modular layout (cleanup normally removes them), nor whether ConfigService's fold renames the v1 files first, which would make has_legacy False.

findings.trigger: Any re-run of perform_real_modular_migration on a directory that already has live data: the C28 retry after a migration died halfway (channels written, containers failed), or F2. Between the two starts the operator saves settings in the panel; save_config writes them into config.json ('the live save target'). The retry calls migrate_system_configs_to_files, which does save_json_func(config.json, main_config) with a fixed six-key dict built from bot_config.json - the operator's settings (heartbeat URL, refresh, debug switch, donation key, folded token/password hash if the fold has run) are replaced wholesale; migrate_channels_to_files overwrites every <id>.json and default.json with the legacy content; migrate_web_configs_to_files resets web_ui.json to the v1 password hash. create_migration_backup copies only config_dir/*.json, so the overwritten channels/*.json and containers/*.json have no backup at all. The log says 'completed successfully'.
findings.suggestion: Make each stage skip targets that already exist (or merge into an existing config.json instead of replacing it), and let create_migration_backup include channels/ and containers/ when they exist. At minimum log loudly which existing files are being replaced.
findings.unsure_why: A re-run needs a preceding partial migration or F2; how often either happens, and whether save_config writes into config.json in the partially migrated state, depends on ConfigService, which I cannot see.

findings.trigger: The operator enters a new Web UI password AND, in the same save, something later in process_config_form fails: the channel files cannot be written (line 620 returns CHANNELS_NOT_SAVED_MESSAGE), save_config raises ConfigServiceError (line 628 returns e.message), or a non-numeric update interval makes int() raise ValueError at line 227 (line 630 returns 'invalid literal for int() ...'). change_web_ui_password() at line 481 has already written the new hash to disk ('The hash and the re-encrypted bot token changed on disk', line 497). All three answers say nothing about the password; two of them read as 'nothing was saved'. The operator's next login with the old password fails and they do not know why.
findings.suggestion: Once password_changed is True, append the 'Web UI password changed; log in again with the new password.' sentence to every return path, including the three failure returns, or perform the password change after the parsing steps that can fail.

findings.trigger: The operator unticks every container's 'Active' checkbox and saves. parse_servers_from_form returns [], 'if servers:' is False, the old list stays in updated_config, save_config succeeds and the answer is 'Configuration saved' - the containers are all still active. Channels have an explicit marker (channel_tables_submitted) to tell 'none' from 'not on this form'; containers have none, so 'none' can never be saved.
findings.suggestion: Add a marker like the channel tables have (e.g. servers_table_submitted) and store [] when it is present, or at least return a visible warning instead of a plain success when the form carried the container table but no selection.
findings.unsure_why: The panel's JS may forbid deselecting the last container, and other callers of process_config_form (without the container table) may rely on the current behaviour - both outside this section.

findings.trigger: A save request reaches process_config_form without a heartbeat_ping_url field. _parse_heartbeat then returns {'enabled': False, 'ping_url': '', 'interval': 5} and line 521 writes it unconditionally: the Status Watchdog is switched off and its secret URL erased, answer 'Configuration saved'. Two plausible senders: the 'other savers' the comment at lines 550-553 mentions ('other savers post no logging fields'), and the ordinary form if the browser omits disabled inputs when the heartbeat section is switched off - which would also break the promise at lines 380-381 that switching off keeps the URL. Servers (line 507) and channels (line 516) are guarded against a form that does not carry them; heartbeat is not.
findings.suggestion: Only replace updated_config['heartbeat'] when the form carries heartbeat fields (heartbeat_ping_url or enableHeartbeatSection); otherwise keep the stored value.
findings.unsure_why: Whether any request without heartbeat fields ever reaches this function depends on the templates, panel.js and the blueprints, none of which are in this section.

findings.trigger: config/server_order.json holds anything but a flat dict of settings: a bare JSON list -> dict.update(list) raises ValueError/TypeError out of load_existing_configs_virtual, which both loaders call last, so the WHOLE configuration fails to load (no containers, no channels, no token); a dict with any key other than 'server_order' (e.g. 'servers' or 'channel_permissions') -> that key silently overwrites the value just assembled from the container and channel files. SPEC Z7 names services/.../server_order.py as the writer of this file and says its reader returns [] on a decode error; this second reader assumes a dict-shaped file and merges it blind.
findings.suggestion: Read the file the way server_order.py does (or via its load_server_order()) and assign only config['server_order'] = <list>, never config.update(<file content>).
findings.unsure_why: server_order.py is not in this section, so I cannot tell what shape it writes; if it always writes {'server_order': [...]} and nothing else, the trigger needs a hand-edited file.

findings.trigger: The operator edits config/config.json or config/channels/<id>.json in place on the host (nano, `cat > file`, a Python json.dump into an existing file - anything that truncates and rewrites the same inode). No directory entry is created, renamed or removed, so neither config_dir's nor channels/'s mtime moves; get_cached_config keeps answering from the cache until restart or an unrelated save. The docstring (lines 81-88) says exactly this case - 'a file edited by hand on the host' - is what the check is for, and the comment at 65-67 itself states the directory-mtime rule that defeats it. Only editors that write-then-rename (vim default, sed -i) are covered.
findings.suggestion: Include the newest file mtime (config.json plus the *.json below channels/ and containers/) in get_config_dir_mtime, or narrow the docstring to 'a file added, removed or replaced by rename'.

findings.trigger: In a channel row the operator types '0', '-5' or 'abc' into the update interval or inactivity timeout. '0' and '-5' pass int() unchanged and are stored (what the status loop does with an interval of 0 or -5 minutes I cannot see); 'abc' raises ValueError, which travels up to line 630 and aborts the whole save with the raw Python text 'invalid literal for int() with base 10: ...' - after the Web UI password change at line 481 has already happened (see F4). The heartbeat interval two methods further down is clamped to 1..60 and falls back on error; these two fields are not.
findings.suggestion: Parse both fields like heartbeat_interval: try/except with a fallback to the previous or default value and a lower bound of 1, and name the row in the message when a value is refused.
findings.unsure_why: The HTML input may carry min=1 and type=number so that browsers never post these values; a direct API call still can.

findings.trigger: A display name that starts with '[' and ends with ']', e.g. '[PROD]' or '[EU] Valheim]'. _parse_display_name treats it as a stringified list: ast.literal_eval fails on '[PROD]' (a name, not a literal), the except branch strips all brackets and quotes and the container is saved as 'PROD'; '[1]' becomes '1'. The panel says saved; the operator typed brackets and got none.
findings.suggestion: Drop the stringified-list heuristic on a string value (the list case is already handled by the isinstance(list) branch above), or apply it only when literal_eval succeeds and yields a list.

findings.trigger: One file in containers/ carries 'order' as a string (a hand edit, or a v1 entry migrated verbatim by migrate_containers_to_files) while the others carry ints. servers.sort(key=order) compares str with int and raises TypeError - outside the per-file try, so load_all_containers_from_files and with it load_real_modular_config fail and no configuration is loaded, because of one field in one file.
findings.suggestion: Normalise the key: key=lambda x: int(x.get('order', 999)) with a try/except fallback to 999, or coerce 'order' per file inside the loop.

findings.trigger: Channel files are written at line 518, config.json only at line 581. When save_config then fails - config.json not writable (e.g. root-owned after a docker exec as root, a case this project has met) while channels/ is - a ConfigServiceError returns 'current_config, False, e.message': the operator is told the save failed, yet the channel permission files are already replaced and the bot loads them at the next reload. Z3 in reverse: a failure is reported for something that partly happened.
findings.suggestion: Write channel files after save_config succeeded, or say in the failure message that the channel permissions were already written.

notes:
Verdict mapping: process_config_form carries F4 as its primary finding; F5, F6 and F13 also belong to that method (one verdict per name, so they are only listed here). F3 is referenced from both perform_real_modular_migration and migrate_system_configs_to_files; F1 from cleanup_legacy_files_after_migration and migrate_web_configs_to_files. No finding IDs F9 (renumbered).

Observations without a trigger I can state (not findings):
- own_actions.window_seconds: get_setting('DDC_DOCKER_CACHE_DURATION', 30) - if utils.settings returns the raw environment string, poll_seconds * 3.5 raises TypeError on every expected_stops() call in the status loop. The docstring reports a live run with the value 120, so presumably it is numeric; utils.settings is not in this section.
- own_actions.note_own_action keys the note by the container string the caller passes; if DockerActionService notes the display name and the watchdog compares docker names, the note never matches. Not visible here.
- config_form_parser_service line 577: the generic loop stores every remaining form value as a string. The debug_level_enabled fix (lines 542-558) shows what happens to a checkbox that panel.js posts as '0'; any OTHER boolean the panel posts as '0' through this loop becomes the truthy string '0'. I cannot name such a key from this section, hence no finding. Same for numeric settings (session_timeout etc.) stored as strings.
- config_form_parser_service lines 224-230 accept only '1','on',True for the per-channel checkboxes while _parse_form_checkbox (line 95) also accepts 'true'/'True'; two truth tests that can drift. Whether the JS ever posts 'true' is not visible.
- config_form_parser_service line 581: message = result.message or 'Configuration saved' also when result.success is False and message is empty; the caller presumably decides by the flag.
- config_form_parser_service: two identical channel-ID validity conditions (lines 213 and 288) must stay in step by hand.
- config_form_parser_service _SKIP_PREFIXES contains 'status_' and 'control_' - any future top-level setting whose name starts so can never be saved through the form.
- config_form_parser_service: the same channel ID in two rows of the SAME table is silently collapsed (last row wins); only cross-table duplicates are reported.
- config_cache_service get_cached_config/set_cached_config copy shallowly; nested dicts/lists (servers, channel_permissions, advanced_settings) are shared between cache and caller. process_config_form is careful to replace rather than mutate them; other callers are not visible.
- config_loader_service line 223-224: default_channel_permissions from config.json is overwritten with {} by config.update(channel_data) and, unlike channel_permissions, never restored in the fallback; only the channels_config.json branch sets it.
- config_loader_service load_all_channels_from_files: an unreadable channel file (loader default {}) becomes an entry {stem: {}} with no 'commands' - the channel appears with no rights and an empty name rather than being reported as broken. What _load_json_file logs is not visible.
- config_loader_service lines 402-404 (virtual layout, ALL_CHANNELS_REMOVED_MARKER) are unreachable: the marker's existence already makes has_real_modular_structure() True.
- config_loader_service load_existing_configs_virtual reads channels_config.json without an exists() check on every load, also in the real layout where cleanup has deleted it; depends on how _load_json_file treats a missing file.
- config_migration_service migrate_channels_to_files writes default.json with commands {serverstatus, command, control, schedule} - a 'command' key nothing else in this section knows, and no 'ss'/'info', which the form parser always writes. Whether default_channel_permissions is consulted anywhere is not visible.
- config_migration_service migrate_legacy_v1_config_if_needed detects a v1 config.json by 'servers' in test_data or 'docker_name' in test_data, on every get_config(). If a modern config.json ever contained a 'servers' key (process_config_form does put servers into updated_config, line 507; whether save_config strips it before writing config.json is not visible), config.json would be renamed away as 'legacy'. Since every install would break, save_config evidently strips it - noted as a dependency, not a finding. Also: if the rename at line 441 fails, the split files exist next to the v1 config.json and the migration repeats on every get_config(), logging an error each time.
- config_migration_service migrate_system_configs_to_files writes auth.json with encryption_enabled: True regardless of whether the v1 bot_token was encrypted (Z9); not decidable here.
- config_migration_service line 300: migrate_containers_to_files does not catch AttributeError (a non-dict server entry), but ensure_modular_structure catches everything, so the start survives; the migration is then retried at every start until the file is fixed, per the C55 rationale.
